Original Requirements: Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Caro game.
Testing Constraints: No manual interaction, GUI, network, or OS-specific behavior
Cover runtime wiring and representative core rules with concise tests
Language Convention Requirements: Use C++17 and CMake only; no external dependencies
Place reusable interfaces in include/*.h and implementations in src/*.cpp pairs
Every header must be self-contained and include all standard headers needed by its declarations
tests/test_main.cpp must include headers only, never implementation .cpp files
Respect a single test target and the exact protocol file names and paths
Keep modules small, cohesive, and avoid circular includes
Domain Reasoning: The core domain is a two-player Caro (five-in-a-row) board played on a finite grid
Moves must be validated: inside bounds and to an empty cell
Turns must alternate strictly between Player X and Player O
Win detection requires scanning lines in four principal directions for sequences of five
Draw occurs when the board is full with no winner
A move history enables undo/reset semantics and auditing of play
The domain engine should be pure logic, independent from I/O, time, or randomness
Runtime entry should only demonstrate the engine without interactive loops
Domain Expectations: Board entity managing dimensions, cell states, and querying/setting cells safely
Game engine that applies validated moves, tracks current player, and updates status
Win detection across horizontal, vertical, and both diagonal directions
Draw detection when all cells are filled and no five-in-row exists
Move history recording applied moves with turn order
Ability to reset the game to initial state
Immutability or copy-safety semantics for read-only queries
Clear error reporting for illegal moves without mutating state
Product Goals: Deliver a clear, testable core Caro game engine with strong correctness
Provide a clean repository structure that compiles and runs using the required protocol
Ensure minimal, robust automated tests validate wiring and key rules
User Stories: As a player, I want the game to reject moves to occupied cells so that rules are respected.
As a player, I want turns to alternate automatically so I don’t need to track whose turn it is.
As a player, I want the game to detect five-in-a-row in any direction to declare a winner.
As a player, I want to reset the board to start a new game quickly.
As a reviewer, I want a non-interactive demo that showcases basic play and exits cleanly.
Competitive Analysis: Classic Gomoku CLI engines: simple, rule-focused implementations with minimal UI
GUI Gomoku/Caro apps: richer UX but often tightly coupled UI and logic
Board game frameworks: generic but may be overkill for focused Caro rules
Educational code samples on five-in-a-row: often incomplete testing and architecture

Requirement Analysis: We must create a C++17 project with strict protocol files and paths, separating pure domain logic (board, rules, engine) from runtime demo and tests. The architecture should enable deterministic, headless tests that cover runtime wiring and representative rules: move validation, alternation, win/draw detection, and reset/history. Files must be small, headers self-contained, and include directions unidirectional to avoid cycles. The runtime entry will run a brief, non-interactive demonstration and exit.
Requirement Pool: Preserve protocol-required files exactly: CMakeLists.txt, src/Main.cpp, tests/test_main.cpp
Implement core Caro mechanics: validation, alternating turns, five-in-a-row, draw
Separate pure domain logic from runtime and tests
Provide concise, deterministic tests covering wiring and one core rule path
Expose move history and reset operations through a stable API
UI / UX / Interaction Design draft: A console-based, non-interactive demo in Main shows a short sequence of valid moves leading to a win or draw, then prints a compact summary and exits. No inputs, loops, or rendering. Tests avoid any real I/O and focus on domain API usage.
Anything UNCLEAR: Default board size for Caro is not specified (common choices: 15x15 or 19x19). Clarify whether variant rules like overline handling, double-three restrictions, or renju constraints apply; current plan assumes simple five-in-a-row wins without special prohibitions.
